pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery learn about Knights & Castles! - DOLPHIN news - Dolphin School
pageCache.text:
Nursery learn about Knights & Castles!
Nursery visited Y2 earlier this week to learn about 'Knights and Castles' - their topic for this half term.
Both year groups had a fantastic time and got so much from the afternoon. The Y2s gave a wonderful, professional presentation, and then all the children looked at and interacted with the castles Y2 had made. The children were even able to see how a bow and arrow worked!
The castles ranged from intricate lego ones to larger structures made from card. Nursery were inspired and returned to their classroom to make castles of their own!

Year 3 had a lovely trip to Reading Museum to see the replica of the Bayeux Tapestry.
The children were challenged to find the scene that they had painted in their Art lessons and were helped to translate the Latin phrases that explain each historical scene.
They delighted the visitors with a beautiful rendition of ‘The night before the battle’ from their production of Gimme the Crown!

pageCache.pageTitle: Winchester Science Museum - DOLPHIN news - Dolphin School
pageCache.text:
Winchester Science Museum
Year 5 Winchester Science Museum Trip Summary
Year 5 enjoyed a fantastic day at the Winchester Science Museum this week, which linked beautifully to our current topic on space and the solar system. The children began by exploring the interactive galleries, where they had the freedom to investigate hands‑on exhibits, test ideas, and discuss their discoveries with one another. Their curiosity and eagerness to engage with each activity set a wonderful tone for the day.
They then took part in the Destination Space workshop, which deepened their understanding of light and its importance in studying space. Students investigated the properties of visible and infrared light by measuring the infrared levels of different coloured cards, discovering how colours absorb or reflect heat differently. They also worked in teams to solve infrared laser mazes using mirrors and light splitters; each successful maze lit up a small infrared detector. This challenge encouraged collaboration, problem‑solving, and perseverance.
To round off the visit, the class enjoyed a planetarium show that transported them through the night sky. They explored familiar constellations and learned new facts about the planets in our solar system, building on the learning we have been doing in class. The children remained enthusiastic throughout the whole experience and represented the school brilliantly. We hope the trip has further ignited their curiosity about space and the wider world of science.

EYFS (Nursery and Reception)
“The Early Years department is superb. The team achieve the perfect balance for the children. They are both professional and warm, focused on each child’s individual learning approach, whilst also instilling a sense of independence and confidence in all children. It really is the perfect foundation for a love of learning. The proof- how happy the children are. My son skips happily into school every day.”
There is a very warm and welcoming feel to the Early Years department at Dolphin. Every child is treated as an individual and the children feel safe and secure in the happy, stimulating environment.
Kindness, making thoughtful personal choices and forming positive relationships with each other is evident when you watch the children at work and play.
Developing a love of learning is the main aim of Jane Robinson and her highly experienced and enthusiastic team. She and her team share a passionate belief that the potential of each child is limitless, and this is shown by the excellent progress every child makes whilst in the team’s care.
Jane found the school for her own children 20 years ago and it inspired her to train as an Early Years teacher.
The children have a wealth of wonderful learning opportunities including visits to the copse, embracing foreign languages, dance, off site trips and working with the older children who inspire them with their caring yet confident attitudes.
The department retains a Montessori ethos yet also embraces current thinking with the child’s ideas and interests placed at the heart of the curriculum.
Jane Robinson, Head of Early Year
"The Early Years staff at Dolphin are calm, patient, and caring. They treat the children as individuals, and take the children’s concerns seriously - from a grazed knee to a homeless flower. They understand that to a small child, the ‘little’ things are ‘big’ things. Our child loves the Forest School at Dolphin, as have we during our visits in the termly Family Week. We are grateful that a school such as Dolphin exists, and that our children have the privilege of attending it."
EYFS Curriculum Overview
There are three prime areas and four specific areas of learning in the EYFS:
Communication and Language
Personal, Social and Emotional Development
Physical Development
Understanding the World
Expressive Arts and Design
Characteristics of Effective Learning
These encapsulate the crucial skills and dispositions that underpin children's learning and development. These Characteristics run through all aspects of our curriculum. By nurturing the Characteristics of Effective Learning, teachers support children in becoming confident, independent learners who are curious, resilient, and passionate about learning. Children in the Early years at Dolphin, learn through both adult-led and child-led experiences.
Our Habits are linked with the Characteristics of Effective Learning. We introduce them in Early Years assemblies, and they are reinforced during the week. We enable children to thrive and grow by recognising success at all levels. We celebrate with the child in the moment by giving them a ‘Dolphin Habit’ certificate. At other times, we celebrate these habits with special praise using specific language. Through this, we see children developing self-confidence, resilience, and emotional well-being.
For more information about our Early Years Dolphin Habits, see below:
The Early Learning Goals
The Early Learning Goals are statutory milestones we must assess children's progress and achievements against at the end of the Reception Year. They encompass the seven areas of learning. Dolphin Nursery teachers are mindful of the goals as they help support the children on their journey towards them. The Early Learning Goals can be found in full at the end of our curriculum.
To provide a challenging and ambitious curriculum.
To foster independence.
To help children become creative and imaginative.
To develop communication skills.
Nursery Curriculum
You can find out more about our Nursery Curriculum here.
In summary, in Dolphin Nursery we aim to inspire children and create in each one: “a true love of learning”.
Reception Curriculum
You can find out more about our Reception curriculum here.
In summary, our Reception curriculum aims to foster holistic development. It aims to empower every child to be confident, curious, resilient, and to love learning!

pageCache.text:
Pre Prep: Nursery to Year 2
In Pre-Prep, learning is rooted in curiosity, play, and self-directed enquiry. The curriculum responds to children’s questions and ideas, encouraging them to explore, investigate, and express themselves confidently within a dialogue-rich environment.
Pupils grow in independence while feeling safe and supported, guided by a central class teacher and enriched by visiting specialists who bring subjects such as Art, Dance, and PE vividly to life. At this age, children begin to develop the Dolphin Habits through certificates for Kind Kangaroos, Persevering Penguins, and Helpful Hippos, helping them reflect on their strengths, build confidence, and cultivate positive learning behaviours.
Through hands-on experiences, collaboration, and guided exploration, children develop a love of learning alongside the foundations of resilience, creativity, and self-motivation.

Inspection Reports
We are delighted to share the final report from our recent ISI visit, with reference to our Material Change Application to teach up to Year 11, starting from September 2026. We are very pleased that the visiting inspectors recognised many of the schools strengths and that the report confirms we are well-prepared to deliver a meaningful and inspiring curriculum via the Middle Years Programme of the IB - Material Change ISI Inspection June 2026
I am delighted to inform you that the feedback from pupil, parent and staff questionnaires was once again fantastic. I was so proud of the 96% ‘Strongly Agree’ or ‘Agree’ response from parents, and pupils and staff were equally positive and supportive in their feedback, with over 90% scores. It was so heartening to see and hear that all three groups within our community value and appreciate everything the school offers, whether academically or pastorally
- Head's comment on Parent Survey Results of ISI Inspection March 2025
Please see below some of the specific and positive feedback we received, from across all of the Sections in our latest ISI Report:
The school’s trips programme ‘enhance[s] pupils’ learning and development across the curriculum.’
We were commended on our ‘varied and well-planned activity programme [Soft Start] at the beginning of the day.’
‘Leaders consistently promote activities to build pupils’ self-confidence and self-esteem.’
Children have ‘wide and varied opportunities to develop their leadership skills by taking on appropriate duties and responsibilities.’
‘Pupils have a clear sense of right and wrong. Teachers trust pupils to behave well and they rise to these high expectations.’
‘Leaders implement an appropriate behaviour policy and have high expectations of pupils’ behaviour.’
‘Pupils feel safe in school.’
‘Leaders have designed a broad and challenging curriculum. Teachers have secure subject knowledge and enable pupils to learn and make good progress.’
‘Teachers have high expectations for pupils.’
Inspection report september 2021I could not have been more pleased with the outcome of our most recent ISI inspection, which makes clear that we are successfully doing what we say we do. Dolphin School really does provide a wonderful and unique all-round education for our boys and girls!
The findings of the EQI Report are as follows:
3.1 - The quality of the pupils’ academic and other achievements is excellent
3.2 - The quality of the pupils’ personal development is excellent
It is the aim of any school to achieve excellent in both categories. I would like to draw your attention to the following highlights under the two headings, as I think these accurately reflect what a Dolphin education is about, and tease out what is so special about this school:
3.1
"Pupils are eager to learn and they make excellent progress across all areas of the curriculum.”
“…they are highly articulate and confident.”
“Pupils’ attitudes to learning are exceptional… .”
“At all ages, pupils are enthusiastic about their studies and talk with gratitude of the support and encouragement they are given by their teachers.”
“Pupils have outstanding speaking skills. From the earliest years they are encouraged to share their opinions and ideas.”
3.2
“Pupils are very well prepared for the next stage of their lives and as they prepare to move on to their next schools.”
“Pupils have a deep appreciation of the non-material aspects of life, nurtured from their earliest years in the woodland environment of the school and frequent reflection they experience in lessons and activities.”
“From an early age, pupils demonstrate a strong sense of right and wrong.”
“Pupils new to the school talked of how they were welcomed and quickly made to feel at home.”
“Pupils delight in making a significant contribution to the school.”
“Pupils demonstrate deep respect for others.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Take One Picture 2026 - DOLPHIN news - Dolphin School
pageCache.text:
Take One Picture 2026
We are thrilled to announce that The National Gallery have chosen Dolphin's Enrichment Project to be part of their Take One Picture exhibition this summer!
This is such an amazing achievement and the children are extremely excited to be showing their art work in the same gallery as Leonardo da Vinci, Raphael and Michelangelo!
Each year the National Gallery chooses one of their paintings to inspire primary school children to create cross-curricular projects. This year's painting was Canaletto's 'A Regatta on the Grand Canal.' The children chose to create a 3D version of the painting, making origami gondolas, Venetian houses out of cardboard boxes and using a marbling technique to create the swirling water of the Grand Canal. The children also made Venetian masks which they wore to the Henley Royal Regatta to compare the 18th century race to our modern day event.
The exhibition will be open to the public from June 4th until 31st August this year, so we hope that you will go and have a look at the incredible Take One Picture exhibition at the National Gallery in London this summer.

pageCache.pageTitle: Lake District Trip - DOLPHIN news - Dolphin School
pageCache.text:
Lake District Trip
Year 6 had an unforgettable adventure in the Lake District, packed with challenge, teamwork, and plenty of fun. The trip began in Whinlatter Forest, where pupils were introduced to the skills of orienteering. Working in small groups, they learned how to read maps, and navigate through the forest, building confidence and problem-solving skills along the way.
One of the highlights was the planned hike up Helvellyn. The group set off with determination, but the weather had other ideas. With gusts reaching 38mph and heavy rain setting in, a sensible and safe decision was made to turn back halfway at Red Tarn. Although they didn’t reach the summit, the experience taught valuable lessons about resilience, risk assessment, and respecting the power of nature. Once safely back down, the group visited the stunning Aira Force waterfalls, where they enjoyed exploring the area and took part in some geocaching activities.
The following day offered two exciting adventures. Half of the group set off on a hike up Catbells, successfully reaching the summit and enjoying breathtaking views across the surrounding landscape. Their efforts were rewarded with a well-deserved ice cream at the end. Meanwhile, the other half took part in an exhilarating ghyll scrambling session down Stoneycroft Ghyll. Pupils worked their way along the stream, taking on a variety of challenges including feet-first slides and jumps, head-first slides, and even some belly flopping into the water. There were smiles and laughter all around—everyone agreed it was a fantastic experience! After lunch, the groups swapped activities so that everyone could enjoy both adventures.
On the final day, the children travelled to Keswick town centre to take part in a competitive treasure trail. Working in teams, they followed clues around the town, finishing on the edge of the beautiful Derwent Water. It was the perfect way to round off a memorable trip.
Overall, the Year 6 Lake District residential was a tremendous success. Pupils showed great enthusiasm, teamwork, and resilience throughout, and returned home with wonderful memories and a real sense of achievement.

NEW Year 9 - Sept 26
Our Offering
Since its inception as a Montessori Nursery school, Dolphin has existed to offer parents a meaningful alternative in an increasingly homogenous educational landscape. Nowhere is this more needful than at Key Stages 3 and 4 (Years 7-11). Schools across the country, whether mixed, single-sex, independent or state, have their academic horizons clipped by the nature of a bloated GCSE curriculum that sees children embarking on these content-heavy courses earlier and earlier. Whilst they may seek to differentiate themselves through sports halls, music practice rooms or computer suites, the reality is that the content of their courses is dictated by an external provider.
Come and see for yourself - Book a tour or taster day for free here.
The impetus behind a full Dolphin secondary education is the desire to give teenagers the same style of holistic, experiential and learner-centred education that younger children already enjoy at the school. For many years, parents have been asking us: "What is the natural progression for my child after Dolphin?" and, for many, there is no real answer. In the context of rising test anxiety, concerns about the validity of the content and even over grade inflation, it is obvious to us that GCSEs will not provide a suitable academic framework for this project, and we are excited choose a different path: the world-renowned International Baccalaureate's Middle Years Programme.
To celebrate this milestone, we are offering up to four full bursaries & scholarships for pupils joining Year 9 September 2026. - Find out more about bursaries & scholarships here
This programme emphasises the development of real-life skills and competencies, enabling staff to design lessons that respond to their own areas of expertise, student interests, and current events. The flexibility of the MYP also allows us to continue to intergrate rich experiential and interdisciplinary learning in our signature day and residential trips programme. These experiences, which are so central to a Dolphin education, promote resilience, flexibility and independence, whilst also fostering those neural connections between abstract concepts and lived experience that helps to actualise learning.
Please scroll down to see our exciting Adventure Trips programme extended to Year 11 and a taste of our concept-based units offering!
If you are interested in finding out more about an inspirational pathway for your child in Years 7-11, please call the school on 01189 341277 or fill out an Enquiry Form.

pageCache.pageTitle: Mission, Aims & Core Values - Dolphin School
pageCache.text:
Mission, Aims & Core Values
Dolphin School’s mission is to guide and inspire children to discover their own unique strengths and talents through learning by experiencing and doing.
We provide a joyful, challenging and stimulating education that nurtures curiosity, confidence and a lifelong love of learning, while celebrating the individuality of every child.
Rooted in our core values — freedom to learn, confidence to be oneself, challenge to excel, discovery through action, and kindness above all — we develop confident, compassionate and independent thinkers who understand that their abilities carry responsibility as well as opportunity. Our pupils learn to accept others for who they are, to think deeply about the world around them, and to act with empathy, integrity and respect.
In alignment with the International Baccalaureate mission, we aim to develop inquiring, knowledgeable and caring young people who appreciate different perspectives and recognise the value of intercultural understanding. By placing learning in real-world contexts and encouraging reflection, collaboration and action, we prepare our students not only for academic success, but to contribute positively to their communities and to a more peaceful, sustainable and interconnected world.
Aims & Core Values
Aims
Provide a challenging, stimulating and broad curriculum
Promote academic, artistic, sporting and cultural excellence
Core Values
These values are promoted, developed and celebrated in our Dolphin Project Qualification Programme, a bespoke series of cross-curricular projects that runs from Years 3-8.
Freedom to learn in my own way
Confidence to be myself
Challenge to excel in what I do
Discovery by doing
Kindness above all

pageCache.text:
Headmaster's Welcome
Dolphin School is unique. It is a school where our core values of Freedom, Discovery, Challenge, Confidence and Kindness are lived out each and every day. Whether it is through our extensive and varied trips programme, our subject specialist teaching from nursery upwards, our lack of uniform, or the first name terms between students and teachers, Dolphin is a school that is different, and proudly so.
Dolphin exists in the image of its founding days. The curriculum is experiential, teachers have the freedom to explore ideas and topics as they arise, and our children are encouraged to be curious, volunteer their own insights and ask questions. Whenever visitors encounter our students in their learning environments, they comment on the genuine enthusiasm shown by our boys and girls, as they vie for the opportunity to tell our guests what they are studying. I always enjoy showing people around Dolphin, where teachers and students do a better job of selling our school than I ever can, just by doing what they do every day of the week!
At the very heart of our educational philosophy is our belief that children learn best when they are happy, when they are comfortable, when they do, when they are free to question and explore. Our children flourish in small classes, in an atmosphere filled with warmth and enthusiasm, where individuality is celebrated and relationships between teacher and child are cherished. We are not constrained to the classroom and strive to maintain a learning environment where our children love coming into school and have the opportunity to learn at their own pace and in their own way. This is what it means to be given Freedom to Learn.
Welcome to Dolphin School.
Adam Hurst, Headmaster

Adventure Trips
The Mountain Adventure Programme at Dolphin is one of the things that truly sets Dolphin apart. Pupils begin with walks on the South Downs in Year 4 and steadily build their skills and confidence, culminating in an eight‑day expedition in the French Alps in Year 8.
Along the way, they take on iconic routes in the Lake District and Snowdonia, while also experiencing an exciting range of increasingly adventurous activities. Coasteering, Via Ferrata's, white‑water rafting, and single‑pitch climbing are just some of the challenges pupils tackle as they progress through the programme.
Beyond exploring beautiful mountain landscapes, children develop essential skills in navigation, camp‑craft, scrambling, and working effectively as part of an expedition team. They return home tired, proud, and with a powerful sense of achievement, often discovering new strengths and capabilities within themselves.
Looking ahead, the programme is set to expand even further, with planned expeditions to the Scottish Highlands, the Dolomites, and Morocco.
Adam Warner Mountain Adventure Programme Coordinator
